# EAFIT is the Antioquia university with the best ESG responsibility in 2022

**This was established in the most recent results of Merco ESG Responsibility carried out by the firm Corporate Reputation Business Monitor (Merco), released on March 1.**

**EAFIT ranked 25th overall (up from 37th in 2021) and fourth in the Education sector. Furthermore, it is the first university outside of Bogotá among the 14 higher education institutions (HEIs) included in the list.**

**Watch the live results** [**here**](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O-mVYxI2s2A) **.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- EAFIT is the Antioquia University with the Best ESG Responsibility in 2022

![Imagen EAFIT is the Antioquia university with the best ESG responsibility in 2022](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/e13a1b36-5b6d-4ff7-adc9-de2b251c4e6e/web/Inventiva-1500.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=7gTJbVZv)

The top 10 companies in Merco Social Responsibility 2022 in Colombia are, in this order, Bancolombia, Grupo Nutresa, Crepes & Waffles, Alpina, Sura, Ecopetrol, Bavaria, Grupo Argos, Arturo Calle and Alquería.

Among the 100 Colombian organizations with the greatest ESG responsibility in 2022 are 14 universities. Among them is EAFIT, which, according to the most recent ranking by the firm Monitor Empresarial de Reputación Corporativa (Merco), is the best higher education institution in Antioquia in this field and the fourth best in the country—the first outside of Bogotá.

“ESG responsibility is always a challenging task, especially for an organization like ours that seeks to impact, create value and transform society through knowledge,” said Claudia Restrepo Montoya, rector of EAFIT, in a message in which she thanked the EAFIT community for their commitment to the actions reflected in Merco ESG Responsibility.

The ranking, which was released on the morning of Wednesday, March 1, measures social responsibility using ESG criteria, which, according to the acronym in English, correspond to _**environmental**_ , **social** (internal sphere, customers and society) and _**governance**_ (ethical and governance sphere).

The inclusion of these criteria in the ranking is recent and, explained Catalina Londoño, Merco's general manager for Colombia, stems from an interest in gathering more and better information, as this allows for a broader range of audiences, metrics, and variables. In the most recent edition, 69,574 surveys were conducted across 24 different information sources.

According to these variables, EAFIT ranked 25th overall, improving its position from the previous edition where it was ranked 37th. The results, stated Isabel Gutiérrez Ramírez, EAFIT's Director of Strategy, "are the result of the University's intentional work focused on the planet's sustainability and the development of humanity. This result confirms that we are on the right track in realizing our vision."

One of the aspects of the ranking that José María San Segundo, CEO of Merco, highlighted is that society perceives organizations' commitment to the environment as insufficient. While acknowledging the increased efforts and investments in this area, he explained this perception by saying that "people's expectations are overshadowing these advances; we have to move very quickly to avoid remaining stagnant, and there are no limits to investment in the environment."

In environmental responsibility (E), EAFIT ranked 25th nationally; 28th in social responsibility (S); and 21st in ethics and governance (G). “These results challenge us to continue adding value through the implementation of good institutional practices. In particular, regarding Corporate Governance, having a solid governance model has allowed us to generate trust and transparency in the decision-making of the different governing bodies, contributing to risk mitigation and the sustainability of the Institution, in line with the University's strategic objectives,” stated María Claudia Gómez Cabana, Acting Secretary General of EAFIT.

Regarding environmental responsibility, Lina Rozo León, Environmental Management Coordinator at the institution, shared that “EAFIT recognizes that one of the challenges of today and the future is to contribute to the well-being of our common home to ensure the continuity of life on the planet. Today more than ever, our stakeholders have expectations and are sensitive to the University's environmental impacts and climate change. Strengthening projects for the Institution in partnership with academia has been crucial so that faculty and students can learn firsthand about the impacts of the university as a park and, together with the Environmental Management Area, carry out projects that involve us all as a community. These partnerships have been fundamental to doing powerful work that extends beyond the university campuses.”
